name: PORTUGAL
lead: Portugal sits at Europe's western edge, where the Atlantic begins. Portuguese sailors once mapped half the globe; their language is spoken by 260 million people today. Famous for golden beaches, fado music, and cork trees supplying half the world's bottle stoppers — its borders are Europe's oldest, nearly unchanged since 1139.

sections.geography: Where the land meets the sea

geo: Portugal stretches down the Iberian Peninsula's western edge with 832 km of Atlantic coastline. The north is green and hilly, soaked by Atlantic rain; the south bakes under Mediterranean sun, with golden cliffs tumbling into turquoise water.

Far offshore, Portugal also owns the Azores — volcanic islands 1,500 km west — and lush Madeira, closer to Morocco than Lisbon. Its highest peak, Mount Pico, is a dormant volcano rising straight from the sea.
animals: The Iberian lynx prowls cork-oak forests on oversized paws, ears swivelling for rabbits. Once nearly extinct (fewer than 100 in 2002), breeding programmes brought it back to over 1,600 animals across Portugal and Spain.

The Iberian wolf — leaner and darker than northern cousins, with striped legs — hunts in small packs through misty highlands north of the Douro. About 300 survive in Portugal, protected by law since 1988.
culture: Blue-and-white azulejo tiles coat church walls, railway stations, and houses — a tradition from Moorish rulers 500 years ago. Fado is music that aches beautifully: one singer, a guitar, and saudade — longing for something you can't quite name.

Football is a religion, with Benfica, Porto, and Sporting in eternal rivalry. The pastéis de nata — a tiny custard tart with a scorched top, invented by Lisbon monks in the 1800s — is eaten by millions daily.
history: Portugal became a kingdom in 1139 — one of Europe's oldest nations. In the 1400s its sailors launched the Age of Discovery: Vasco da Gama reached India by sea; Pedro Álvares Cabral landed in Brazil. The empire spanned four continents.

The 1755 Lisbon earthquake flattened the capital and triggered a tsunami felt across Europe. The city was rebuilt in a bold grid within years. In 1974 the peaceful Carnation Revolution ended dictatorship — named for flowers placed in soldiers' rifle barrels.
wows: Portugal produces roughly half the world's cork, stripped from living trees by hand every nine years.
Lisbon was founded around 1200 BC — four centuries before Rome was even built.
In early 2025 Portugal generated over 80% of its electricity from renewables in a single quarter.
The world's oldest operating bookshop, Livraria Bertrand in Lisbon, has been open since 1732.
Portugal's borders have barely shifted since 1139 — oldest in continental Europe.
Portuguese is the official language of nine countries across four continents.
The 1974 Carnation Revolution was so peaceful that protesters placed flowers in soldiers' rifle barrels.

myths.myth: Portugal is always warm and sunny
myths.fact: Porto is wetter than London in winter. Heavy Atlantic rain soaks the north; even the Algarve gets rainy spells. Only the far south earns the postcard weather.

myths.myth: Portuguese is just Spanish with an accent
myths.fact: They share Latin roots but sound very different. A Spanish speaker cannot automatically understand European Portuguese — the two are distinct languages.
